capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: 60.0 kWh nominal, CATL LFP (EV Database 2021-23 RWD; the existing OpenEV import for the 2026 Premium-I also shows 60/57). evspecifications lists 62 kWh for 2023-24, Wikipedia 64 kWh for the current RWD. Carried over from the 2021-2023 LFP RWD (EV Database); Highland RWD keeps the 170 kW peak (InsideEVs).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: 57.0 kWh usable (EV Database estimate). Carried over from the 2021-2023 LFP RWD (EV Database); Highland RWD keeps the 170 kW peak (InsideEVs).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: LFP (CATL); evspecifications 2023/2024 RWD LFP. Carried over from the 2021-2023 LFP RWD (EV Database); Highland RWD keeps the 170 kW peak (InsideEVs).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: 400 V architecture (EV Database); evspecifications 345 V nominal. Carried over from the 2021-2023 LFP RWD (EV Database); Highland RWD keeps the 170 kW peak (InsideEVs).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Tesla's release note (2020.24.6.4, Model S/3/X/Y) says the car preconditions its battery when navigating to a fast charger; this is a software feature delivered to the whole Model 3 line (2024 RWD). Page mentions no manual battery-warming control. A manual control was neither found nor ruled out: Tesla's owner's manual pages were blocked (403) and scheduled-departure preconditioning in search excerpts is cabin-oriented.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: 170 kW (EV Database; evspecifications 2023 and 2024 RWD 170 kW; InsideEVs Highland: RWD 170 kW unchanged). Carried over from the 2021-2023 LFP RWD (EV Database); Highland RWD keeps the 170 kW peak (InsideEVs).

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: the existing OpenEV data for the 2026 Canadian Premium-I (same Highland LFP RWD hardware) shows 11 kW and EV Database lists 11 kW (3-phase, EU) for the LFP RWD; Basenor/Wikipedia 7.6 kW (32 A) is for the older RWD (2017-2023), so a lower single-phase North American limit is possible.
